question.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ at the point where $(\frac{\pi }{8},\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
The slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ is given by ${f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{8}).$

We will calculate ${f}^{′}(x)$ using the chain rule. First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
y=\operatorname{sin}⁡u,\,u=2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡u)\cdot (2) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi }{8},$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ is $\sqrt{2}.$
